ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Mary Seacole — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Three-month review after chlorthalidone was stopped: blood pressure above target, losartan added; lipids on atorvastatin; knee and falls

text.paragraph: Three-month review after chlorthalidone was stopped. [S]

Mary Seacole returns five weeks after the sick visit, when chlorthalidone was stopped for a low sodium. The dizziness on standing went within two days, she ate normally once the cold passed, and she has had no further near-falls. The sodium recheck planned for a week after that visit did not happen: she felt well, and the trip to the laboratory by bus with her knees seemed too much for a single blood test. On amlodipine alone her home readings average 140/82, and her ankles swell a little by evening. She has finished the physical therapy course and goes to the tai chi class twice a week. Her knees are better; she asked about an injection but would rather keep to exercise, her own massage and the gel for now. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1877-06-15; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; blood pressure 144/84 seated, 140/82 standing at three minutes, pulse 74; weight 77.2 kg
No knee effusion; Timed Up and Go 13 seconds with the cane

Headaches on waking for three weeks and blood pressure 184/102 mmHg at the visit (average of two seated readings with a large cuff); no chest pain, breathlessness, visual loss, confusion or weakness; fundi with arteriolar narrowing but no hemorrhages or papilledema; no hypertensive emergency; hypertension not yet confirmed
S — Synthetic presenting problem; resolved into stage 2 hypertension when a week of home readings confirmed it. Not a claim about her real health.

Stage 2 hypertension confirmed by home readings (seven-day average 168/96 mmHg), with left ventricular hypertrophy by ECG voltage; no albuminuria; 10-year cardiovascular risk about 14%; treated to reduce the risk of stroke, heart failure and kidney disease

S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the second visit. It is linked to the recorded apoplexy before her death only as the reason for the stroke-prevention teaching; the record does not claim that she had hypertension.

Bilateral primary knee osteoarthritis, worse on the left: pain on stairs and on rising from a chair, morning stiffness under 30 minutes, crepitus and bony enlargement without warmth; clinical diagnosis without imaging
S — Synthetic modern problem; not a claim about her real health.
Fall risk: one fall in the past year, a trip on the outside steps without injury; afraid of falling and going out less; STEADI screen positive; Timed Up and Go 15 seconds
Obesity, class 1 (BMI 31.6); she calls herself stout and wants to lose some weight for her knees
S — Synthetic modern problem; her self-description as stout is documented, her weight is not.

Thiazide-associated hyponatremia (sodium 129 mmol/L) and hypokalemia (potassium 3.3 mmol/L) with orthostatic hypotension and a near-fall, after four days of a cold with little food while taking chlorthalidone; no confusion; resolved after chlorthalidone was stopped
S — Synthetic adverse drug event at an unscheduled visit; a common effect of thiazide diuretics in older women, not a historical diagnosis.

Stage 2 hypertension (I10). Above target on amlodipine alone, 144/84 in the clinic and 140/82 at home. Raising amlodipine would worsen the ankle swelling, so an angiotensin receptor blocker is added; it does not lower sodium. LDL 82 mg/dL on atorvastatin, down 44%. [S]
Losartan 25 mg daily with amlodipine 5 mg.

Blood tests drawn at home by the community nurse whenever a separate trip would be needed.

tr.td: Blood pressure in the clinic (seated, large cuff, two readings) and at home; target below 130/80 mmHg
Weight and BMI (5% weight-loss goal for knee osteoarthritis)
One week after a low sodium, then as for the medicines

The sodium and potassium recheck due one week after the sick visit was missed: she felt well, and the bus trip to the laboratory with her knees seemed too much for one test. Today, five weeks after chlorthalidone was stopped, sodium is 138 mmol/L, potassium 4.2 and creatinine 0.94 mg/dL (eGFR 65), all normal, and she has had no symptoms, so no harm resulted. Corrective action: blood tests are drawn at home by the community nurse when a separate trip would be needed
Four to twelve weeks after starting a statin, then yearly
